clue.text: Start in parliament, no gent returning can

indicators.note: the start of the word parliament gives its opening letter
returning tells us the words no and gent (as a title) are read backwards together

parts.note: a gent may be addressed as sir

explanation.surface: Someone at the opening of parliament, with no gentleman coming back, perhaps carrying a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NO + SIR as one run, giving RISON after P. 'Can' is slang for a jail, the puzzle's running theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is American slang for a jail.

clue.text: Trap a Burmese gentleman in garden feature

indicators.note: in says the title goes inside the water feature

parts.note: a pond is a feature of many gardens
U is a Burmese honorific for a man, like Mr

explanation.surface: Catching a man from Myanmar in an ornamental pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for stray animals, so a trap or place of confinement.

clue.text: One unravelling serial descriptive of foreign national

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: unravelling suggests the letters of serial are untangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone untangling a television serial that depicts an overseas citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective describing a citizen of a Middle Eastern state.

clue.text: Went from second to third? Clearly a game of chance, mostly

parts.note: overt means openly or clearly visible

indicators.note: mostly means the game's name loses its final letter

parts.note: keno is a lottery-style game of chance

explanation.surface: A motorist moves up a gear, apparently gambling on most of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went from second to third' suggests gear changes, but it is a race: being passed drops you a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner passed by a rival slips down one place in the race order.

clue.text: A place of confinement almost cut something crucial

indicators.note: almost means the synonym for cut loses its final letter

parts.note: to chop is to cut
a key factor is something crucial

explanation.surface: A prison cell nearly severed something vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CHOP to CHO. CHOKEY is British slang for prison, from Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: Chokey is old British slang for a jail or lock-up.

clue.text: Optimist put small house on each

parts.note: ho is the short form of house
per means each, as in so much per person

explanation.surface: A positive thinker builds a little home on every plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hopes is an optimist.

clue.text: Saying cauliflower head is hard in Middle Eastern language

indicators.note: saying signals that the assembled pieces are spoken and give a word of the same sound

parts.note: the curd is the white head of a cauliflower, then is, then H for hard

explanation.surface: Claiming a vegetable's top is tough in some regional tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of an ethnic people across Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

clue.text: Lonely dig moves to the sound of singing

indicators.note: moves suggests the letters of lonely dig shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A solitary excavation shifts to the accompaniment of music.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine style of song swinging between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Argue in the capacity of right relative

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived English for 'in the capacity of'

explanation.surface: Disputing with a proper relation in some official role.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to have a dispute or row.

clue.text: Dear pug changes into one of better sort

indicators.note: changes says the letters of dear and pug are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beloved pug dog turns into a superior specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: An improved model or version is something of a better sort.

clue.text: Present soldiers with last of armament handling

parts.note: to treat someone is to present them with something
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of armament

explanation.surface: Giving troops a gift with the end of their weaponry.
explanation.definitionFit: The way something is dealt with or managed.

clue.text: Dave travelled to return anew, a lover of excitement

indicators.note: travelled hints that the letters of Dave and return move about; 'anew' reinforces the remaking

explanation.surface: Dave made a journey so he could come back fresh, being a thrill-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'anew' are surface padding; DAVE and RETURN together give exactly the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person drawn to risk and daring exploits loves excitement.

clue.text: While away time? I would with the French

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether to pass the time, saying they would, with the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf about doing nothing is to while away time.

clue.text: Spend time here, caught by connection

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A suggestion to pass time somewhere, having been caught out by a contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend time' is the prison sense of doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a jail, where a prisoner serves a sentence.

clue.text: Something to give a nag the brush off!

definitions.text: Something to give a nag the brush off!

parts.words: Something to give a nag the brush off!
parts.note: read as a rebuff to a nagging person, but a nag is a horse being brushed down with a grooming tool

explanation.surface: Something to dismiss a persistent complainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed grooming tool used on horses' coats.

clue.text: A jolly church song is something to sink into easily

parts.note: a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A cheerful hymn is pleasant and easy to lose yourself in.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded seat with side supports is one you settle back into.

clue.text: Unbelievably I'm facing old VIP

indicators.note: unbelievably suggests the letters of I'm facing are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: Incredibly, I am confronting an elderly bigwig.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee or important person, originally a Venetian magnate.

clue.text: Numbers on a giro returned for Herb

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the numbers come last in the down-style order
returned says the word giro is read backwards

parts.note: Num is the abbreviation for the Bible book Numbers

explanation.surface: Figures printed on a welfare giro sent back, made out to someone called Herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns GIRO into ORIG; 'on' puts NUM after A. A giro is a British benefit payment cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Origanum is the plant genus of marjoram and oregano, used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Something beneficial traps engineer

parts.note: a gin is a snare, so gins are traps

explanation.surface: A useful thing ensnares a technician.
explanation.definitionFit: A root prized as a tonic for health.

clue.text: Keep quiet about United with large jug

indicators.note: about says the gag goes around the other letters

parts.note: to gag someone is to make them keep quiet

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay silent about a football club with a big pitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is British slang for prison, not a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet labour camp, and so a prison, which is what jug means in slang.

clue.text: Some Cadillac UN allowed to keep, having holes

indicators.note: some indicates just part of the words Cadillac UN allowed is taken

explanation.surface: A UN official is permitted to retain part of a luxury car riddled with gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to gaps or missing portions.

clue.text: Song from the Yemen alternatively

indicators.note: alternatively means every other letter of the words the Yemen is taken

explanation.surface: A tune originating in the Arabian state, or perhaps another option.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of THEYEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious song of praise.

clue.text: Appropriate accent is of broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests the letters of accent is of are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A suitable intonation is one fit for radio transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to seize or take officially, a verb.

clue.text: Dog Common's leader or soldier?

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Common's

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Asking if a dog belongs to the Commons chief or is a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged Welsh breed, the British royal family's favourite.

clue.text: Keep tug

definitions.meaning: a keep is the fortified central stronghold of a castle
a tug boat hauls other vessels

explanation.definitionFit: A tall fortified building like a castle stronghold, and also one that hauls vessels along.

clue.text: Prepare for attack from a former cast

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters of a former are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting ready to fight using an ex-member of the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm in advance against expected trouble.

clue.text: Minute present is for little fish

parts.note: now means the present time
's is the contracted form of is

explanation.surface: A tiny gift intended for small fry.
explanation.definitionFit: Small freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Boating when the heart is missing could be pokey

indicators.note: could be signals the remaining letters can be rearranged
the heart is the central letter of boating, which is dropped

explanation.surface: Messing about in boats without enthusiasm can feel cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the middle T from BOATING leaves BOAING, rearranged. 'Pokey' is American slang for jail, not small.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagnio was a Turkish prison or bathhouse; pokey is slang for a jail.

clue.text: Stir spritzer

definitions.meaning: a wine spritzer is a long chilled drink of the cooling kind

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a jail cell, and also a long iced drink of wine mixed with soda or juice.
